feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — Tenure is not a material artifact, but an institutional designation.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not modeled on biological systems.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not a load-bearing or mechanical construct.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — The status is visible via role or title, but the system is abstract.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Represented in documents or systems, but not material in itself.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It operates through policy and procedure, not autonomous action.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Built as a deliberate structure for career advancement, protection, and labor segmentation.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Triggers downstream consequences, but is not itself an output engine.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Does not perform logical operations or data transformation.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — It changes external status, but has no intrinsic state logic.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Engages people, but is not an interactive interface.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Institutionalized but not embedded in computational architecture.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Dependent on ongoing institutional participation and enforcement.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Not necessary for all educational or employment systems.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Represents a lasting endorsement of scholarly legitimacy and autonomy.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Serves as a public signal of institutional trust, prestige, and career stability.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Bound by highly formalized procedures (reviews, documentation, votes).
feedback.Compositional: Excluded — Structured, but not composed of modular, semantically independent parts.
feedback.Normative: Included — Encodes expectations about merit, conduct, and professional duty.
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not reference itself or legal form.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Defined by a fixed review window and conferred for an open-ended term.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Tracked and maintained in administrative software and policy databases.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists through shared institutional and professional belief structures.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Defined by universities, legislatures, and labor agreements.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Conveys identity status within academic or legal hierarchies.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Controlled by procedures, laws, collective bargaining rules.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Determines salary, job security, and long-term resource allocation.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Subject to ongoing public debates over privilege, access, and reform.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Involves formalized progression, review, committee deliberation, and ceremonial acknowledgment.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises persistent ethical questions around fairness, exclusivity, and accountability.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the tenure system as a symbolic, rule-governed, and regulated institutional construct. It is temporal in structure, ritualized in process, and significant across political, ethical, and economic dimensions. Though abstract, its social power and symbolic weight make it a system-critical mechanism in professional contexts.
